# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 3 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 3
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. For again he says to them concerning these things: "Why do you fast to me? says the Lord. So that your voice may be heard today with a shout? This is not the fast I have chosen, says the Lord — not a person humbling his soul.
2. Not even if you bend your neck as a hoop and put on sackcloth and heap on ashes — not even then shall you call it an acceptable fast."
3. But to us he says: "This is the fast I have chosen, says the Lord: Loose every chain of unrighteousness, untie the bands of violent dealing, send away the broken by release, and tear apart every unjust agreement.
4. Break your bread for the hungry and, if you see a naked man, clothe him; bring the homeless into your house, and if you see a lowly person, do not despise him — neither you yourself nor any of your household.
5. Then shall your light break forth early, and your healing shall arise quickly, and righteousness shall go before you, and the glory of God shall surround you.
6. Then you shall cry and God shall hear you, and while you are still speaking he shall say: 'Here I am.'"
7. How great a benefit it is, brothers, that the Lord has shown us these things and speaks to us, declaring what kind of fasting he requires! And the Lord's service is sweet and glorious and brought to us.

*[Note: This is Barnabas's commentary on Isaiah 58:4-10 as read through the LXX.]*
